# Clutch — machining sheet (generated by mechanical/clutch/clutch.py)

All dimensions mm. **Bold** = critical for concentricity or the magnetic gaps: turn these in ONE chucking.
Magnetic parts: low-carbon steel (1018/1020/12L14), anneal after machining if possible. Never 300-series stainless.

## Field housing (steel) — `field_housing.step`
| Feature | Dimension | Tolerance / note |
|---|---|---|
| OD | **Ø80.0** | h7 (cover spigot fits over it) |
| Length | 20.0 | ±0.05 — sets the 0.3 mm rotor face gap |
| Motor pilot recess (back) | **Ø38.1 (measure your motor) × 2.0 deep** | slide fit on the pilot, ≤0.02 play; the model shows +0.2 |
| Inner pole bore | **Ø19.2** through | concentric with OD and pilot within 0.03 |
| Coil cavity | Ø28.0 … Ø54.0, 15.0 deep from the front | |
| Back plate | 5.0 thick | |
| Motor screws | 4× Ø5.5 thru on 47.14 square, c'bore Ø9 from front to z=6 | M5×30 SHCS + nuts behind the motor flange |
| Coil leads | Ø3.2 thru at r=20.5 + 3.2×1.5 groove on the back face | |
| Cover screws | 3× M4 radial at 120°, 14 from the back face | |

| Tooth ring | r 32.0 … 38.0, 30 teeth (12.0° pitch), 0.90 high, flank 30° from axis | roots 0.5 below the pole face; see teeth notes |

## Other parts
- Output shaft: Ø12 h6 ground rod × 78, 0.6 deep flat × 22 at the pulley end.
- Leaf springs: 3× 0.3 mm blue spring-steel shim, 8 wide, holes Ø3.3 at 21.2 centres.
- Spacers: 3× Ø7 × 3.5, Ø3.3 hole (steel or brass).
- Coil: ~850 turns 0.32 mm (AWG 28) enamelled Cu on a bobbin Ø28.6…Ø53.4 × 14.5; ≈24 Ω. Leads out through the back plate.
- Bearings: 2× 6001-2RS. Screws: 4× M5×30 + nuts, 3× M4×8, 6× M3×6 low-head, 1× M3×8.

## Teeth
- 30 radial teeth, true angular profile: equal tip and root lands, flanks 30° from the axis at the mean radius.
- Engaged pole gap 0.15, stroke 1.1 -> released gap 1.25.
- Machine both rings with the same CAM program and tool, in the same setup orientation, then lap them together.
- Flanks: 3D finishing with a small ball end mill (Ø1–2) or a chamfer mill whose half-angle equals the flank angle
  (30° flank -> 60° chamfer mill / V-bit; set `flank_deg = 45` for a standard 90° chamfer mill — the cam-out force
  then rises ~1.8x, so expect ~1.3x more hold current; re-calibrate per design.md §7.4).
